name: AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes
description: A large and varied database of human motion that unifies 15 different optical marker-based mocap datasets by representing them within a common framework and parameterization using SMPL body models. The dataset contains over 40 hours of motion data, spanning over 300 subjects and more than 11,000 motions.
citeAs: Naureen Mahmood, Nima Ghorbani, Nikolaus F. Troje, Gerard Pons-Moll, Michael J. Black. AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes. arXiv:1904.03278v1 [cs.CV] 5 Apr 2019
rai:dataCollection: AMASS unifies 15 existing optical marker-based motion capture datasets by converting mocap data into realistic 3D human meshes using the MoSh++ method. The source datasets contain varying markersets ranging in size from 37 to 91 markers.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Physical data collection, Direct measurement
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: During a mocap session, markers may get occluded by the body due to pose. If multiple markers of a particular body part are occluded simultaneously, the optimization may result in unreliable and implausible poses. A weight-balancing factor q is introduced to adjust the pose prior weight as a factor of the number of missing markers.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The dataset combines 15 existing motion capture datasets: ACCAD, BioMotion Lab, CMU, EKUT, Eyes Japan, HumanEva, KIT, MPI HDM05, MPI Limits, MPI MoSh, SFU, SSM, TCD Hand, TotalCapture, and Transitions. Each dataset was recorded using different numbers of markers placed at different locations on the body.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: MoSh++ converts mocap marker data into SMPL body model parameters through a two-stage optimization process. Stage I optimizes poses, shape, and latent marker positions for randomly chosen frames. Stage II optimizes pose and soft-tissue deformation coefficients for each frame while keeping latent marker locations and body shape parameters constant.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The method uses MoSh++ to fit the SMPL/DMPL body model to observed mocap markers. The optimization includes data terms measuring distance between simulated and observed markers, shape priors, pose regularization, hand pose regularization, temporal smoothness terms, and soft-tissue deformation priors. Hyperparameters were tuned using cross-validation on the SSM dataset.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: MoSh++ method using SMPL body model, DMPL for soft-tissue dynamics, and MANO hand model. Implementation uses Powell's gradient based dogleg minimization in the Chumpy autodifferentiation package.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will be publicly available to the research community at http://amass.is.tue.mpg.de. The authors will support the community in adding new captures as long as they can be similarly shared and will continue to expand the dataset.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset captures body shape variations across 346 subjects. Two of the three subjects in the SSM dataset were professional models who signed modeling contracts allowing release of their 4D scan data.
rai:dataUseCases: The consistent representation of AMASS makes it readily useful for animation, visualization, and generating training data for deep learning. The dataset can be used for training computer vision algorithms, with SMPL providing a standard skeletal representation and fully rigged surface mesh compatible with most game engines and graphics packages.
